subject: Hierarchical Model with Covariates and Autoregressive Structure

messages.author: 5885eeaed6019ff2
messages.subject: Hierarchical Model with Covariates and Autoregressive Structure
parts:
This is my first attempt at Stan. After a day of learning, copy-pasting from others and debugging, I fitted a hierarchical model with covariates in the hierarchy. However, as soon as I define the hierarchy as an autoregressive process plus covariates, the model fails to capture the true values. I believe it could be an identification problem but I don't quite see it. 

The general model predicts Nx1 observations Y, with predictors K predictors in matrix X (N x K). The observations are grouped into H "households" indexed by a variable "id". The structure is similar to the radon example in Gelman and Jill. 
Y_n = X_n beta[id[n]] + error_n
For each household h, there is a set of coefficients (intercept and slope), beta[h] ~ Normal (mu_beta, sigma_beta) . Each beta[h] is a K dimensional vector.
I introduced covariates such that one of the coefficients is affected by variables Z. In particular beta[h, K] ~ Normal (mu_beta + Z*delta, sigma_beta). So changes in the exogenous variable Z, can change the slope beta[K] for each household. Z varies by observation. This works (see code attached). What does not work is when I define the hierarchical equation (the "state" equation) as an autoregressive process. 

Below is the code to create the synthetic dataset and run the model. 

# Create a dataset with H households
# response Y depends on intercept and two covariates x1, x2
# Y_i = b0 + b1_i*x1 + b2_i*x2 + e_y
# e_y ~ N(0, sigma_y)
# b1 ~ N(3, 2^2)
# b2 ~ N(5, 1^2)
# b3 ~ N(-5 + b3[t-1] +delta_1*Z1 + delta_2*Z2, 2^2) # with autoregression
# delta = c(2,-2)
# X contains the intercept and drawn from uniform [1, uniform, uniform]
# Z is also generated from the uniform. 


# Set Seed
set.seed(1408)
# Number of households
H = 200

mu.b     = c(3, 5, -5)
sigma.b  = c(2, 1, .2)
delta    = c(.5,-.5) # effect delta is constant across Households
theta    = 0.8

# create vectors for the true parameters 
b =  matrix(0, nrow = H, ncol = 3)
kk = 0

Ni = sample(8:20, H, replace = TRUE) # each household has different number of observations
id = as.vector(matrix(0, sum(Ni), 1))

x  = matrix(0, sum(Ni), 3)
z  = matrix(0, sum(Ni), 2)
y  = as.vector(matrix(0, sum(Ni), 1))

# Simulate Data
for(i in 1:H) {
  b[i,1] = rnorm(1, mu.b[1], sigma.b[1])
  b[i,2] = rnorm(1, mu.b[2], sigma.b[2])
  b[i,3] = rnorm(1, mu.b[3], sigma.b[3])
  for(j in 1:Ni[i]) {
    kk = kk + 1
    x[kk, ] = c(1, runif(2))   # the x covariates are Unif(0,1)
    z[kk, ] = runif(2)   # the z covariates are Unif(0,1)
    if(j==1){
      btemp = b[i, 3]
    } else {
      btemp = theta*btemp + delta[1]*z[kk, 1] + delta[2]*z[kk, 2] + rnorm(1,0, sigma.b[3]) 
    }
    y[kk] = b[i,1] + b[i,2]*x[kk, 2] + b3temp*x[kk, 3] + rnorm(1, 0, 1)
    id[kk] = i 
    }
  }

# Here comes the Stan Code
myhiercode ="
data {
  int<lower=0> N; // observations
  int<lower=0> K; // parameters of obs equation
  int<lower=0> J; // parameters of state equation
  int<lower=0, upper=200> id[N]; // identifier of household
  int<lower=0> H;  // number of households
  matrix[N, K] X; // regressors of obs equation
  matrix[N, J] Z; // regressors of state equation
  vector[N] Y;    // outcomes
}

parameters {
  vector[(K-1)] b[H];
  vector[K] mu_b;
  vector[N] b3;
  vector[J] delta;
  vector<lower=0, upper = 10>[K] sigma_b;
  vector<lower=0, upper = 10>[J] sigma_delta;
  real<lower=0, upper = 100> sigma_Y;
  real<lower=0, upper = 1> theta;
  }
  
model {
  // priors
  sigma_Y ~ uniform(0, 100);
  theta ~ beta(1, 1);
  for (k in 1:K){
    mu_b[k] ~ normal(0, 10);
    sigma_b[k] ~ uniform(0,100);
  }
  
  for (j in 1:J){
    sigma_delta[j] ~ uniform(0,10);
    delta[j] ~ normal(0, sigma_delta[j]);
  }
  
  for (h in 1:H){
    b[h, 1] ~ normal(mu_b[1], sigma_b[1]);
    b[h, 2] ~ normal(mu_b[2], sigma_b[2]);
    }
    b3[1] ~ normal(mu_b[3]+Z[1]*delta, sigma_b[3]);
  for (n in 2:N){
    b3[n] ~ normal(b3[n-1]*theta + Z[n]*delta, sigma_b[3]);
   }  
  for (n in 1:N)
    Y[n] ~ normal(X[n,1]*b[id[n],1] + X[n,2]*b[id[n],2] + X[n,3]*b3[n], sigma_Y);
}
"

dat = list(N = length(y), H = dim(b)[1], K= ncol(x), J = ncol(z), Y=y, X=x, Z=z, id=id)
myhlm = stan(model_name="Hierarchical Linear Model", model_code = myhiercode, data=dat , iter = 200, chains = 1, verbose = FALSE)

The model recover the parameters except for delta and some of the sigmas. If I avoid the autoregressive structure, the model recovers all parameters very well even with 200 iterations.  
What is it about the autoregressive structure of b3 that generates the problem? Is it identification? Or just a problem of these kind of hierarchical models with autoregression?
